# Regreenity — Public Product Reference

Regreenity is a PlanetHike OÜ project for cruise-line passenger experience. It is designed as a white-label interaction layer inside the cruise line's existing app rather than as a separate consumer social network.

## Core product areas

### Passenger experience
- Opt-in, positive guest interaction designed for the cruise line's existing app.
- Guardrails support respectful first contact and public onboard experiences.

### Crew recognition
- Guests frame the crew member and visible badge while the service moment is fresh; a crew-participating selfie is also supported.
- When duplicate names make text insufficient, the operator's identity service may perform face matching under its own approved biometric controls.
- Images, biometric templates, candidate lists and match scores remain on-device, ship-local or in cruise-line systems; Regreenity never receives them.
- Recognition uses prepared positive reasons and avoids public crew rankings.

### Service recovery
- Guests receive a private route to signal friction during the sailing.
- Experience Pulse supports timely service feedback and outcome measurement.

### Engagement and ancillary discovery
- Voluntary interests and onboard context can surface relevant activities or experiences.
- The cruise line retains inventory, pricing, checkout, payment and fulfilment.
- Live-event feedback uses three to five structured questions and prepared response blocks without free text.
- Authorized leaders receive immediate aggregate feedback; the cruise line controls publication.

### Aggregate-only measurement
- The default architecture has no Regreenity passenger/crew source-event analytics endpoint.
- A cruise-line or ship-local privacy gateway sends only a predefined aggregate report covering activation, recognition, structured ratings, recovery and net attributed revenue.
- Names, passenger or crew identifiers, photos, booking/attribution references, exact event timestamps, free text and payment data cannot enter that report.
- Randomized or hashed person-level identifiers are also excluded because pseudonymous data may remain personal data.
- Non-identifying service-health totals may include uptime, latency buckets, sync success, deployed version and error counts.
- The default minimum reporting group is 20; smaller cells are suppressed or rolled up before transmission.
- Cross-customer benchmarks use ranges or percentiles across at least five independently operated sailings and 100 qualifying responses, and customers may opt out.

## Integration
- Regreenity is designed as an add-on to the cruise line's existing guest app and operating systems.
- Integration, security and deployment details are agreed directly with each cruise line and are not published in this public reference.

## Product and evidence boundaries
- Regreenity is not a cruise operator, booking engine, merchant, unrestricted chat service or dating app.
- Public demonstrations and metrics are illustrative and do not imply a cruise-line affiliation.
- The public interactive walkthrough uses illustrative data and is not a production deployment.
- Performance claims should follow real pilot evidence.
- Minimised and anonymised analytics reduce privacy risk but are not described as "privacy-free" or "compliance-free."
